subject: antlion larva
title: This Insect Doesn't Poop for Up to 3 Years

scenes.text: This insect can go three years without pooping.
It's an antlion larva, waiting at the bottom of a sand pit it digs in about 15 minutes.
When an ant slips in, it flicks sand to knock it down the slope, then grabs it.
But its gut is a dead end. There's no way out, so every meal's waste stays inside.
It can stay a larva for up to three years, storing all of it.
It finally empties out only at the end of its cocoon stage, as it becomes a winged adult.

description:
Antlion larvae dig cone-shaped pits in sand and pelt prey with flicked sand. Their midgut ends in a dead end, so waste builds up through the whole larval stage, which can last up to three years.
The gut only connects near the end of the pupal stage, and the stored waste is passed as the adult emerges.
Would you rather have this or the wombat's cube poop?
first_comment: Some of the stored waste even gets turned into silk for its cocoon. Did you ever make antlion pits as a kid?
